record.paper_title: Some open problems in dynamical systems
record.original_question: Consider the spatial n-body problem with n ≥ 3 after fixing the center of mass at 0 and performing the paper's smooth time-reparametrization to obtain a complete flow generated by H_e on the energy surface H_e^{-1}(0). For every energy value e, is the nonwandering set of the Hamiltonian flow of H_e nowhere dense in H_e^{-1}(0)?

evidence.quote: 7.3 - Following G.D. Birkhoﬀ ... Question. Is for every e the non wandering set of the Hamiltonian ﬂow of He on H−1 e (0) nowhere dense in H−1 e (0) ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Newtonian spatial $n$-body problem with $n \geq 3$: point masses $m_1, \dots, m_n > 0$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$ with positions $q_i$ interacting via the Newtonian potential $U(q) = \sum_{i<j} m_i m_j / |q_i - q_j|$, with Hamiltonian $H(q,p) = \sum_i |p_i|^2/(2m_i) - U(q)$. Fix the center of mass at the origin and pass to the standard reduced phase space. After a smooth time reparametrization that slows time near collisions so as to extend the flow to a complete smooth flow on each energy hypersurface (replacing $H$ by an equivalent Hamiltonian $H_e$ on the level $H_e^{-1}(0)$ corresponding to the original energy $e$), one obtains a complete Hamiltonian flow on $H_e^{-1}(0)$.

Recall that a point $x$ is nonwandering for a flow $\phi^t$ if for every neighborhood $U$ of $x$ and every $T>0$ there exists $t > T$ with $\phi^t(U) \cap U \neq \emptyset$. Let $\Omega(e) \subset H_e^{-1}(0)$ denote the nonwandering set of the reparametrized flow.

Question: For every real value of the energy $e$, is $\Omega(e)$ nowhere dense in $H_e^{-1}(0)$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question, attributed by Herman to Birkhoff and Kolmogorov and described as one of the oldest problems on the Newtonian n-body problem, remains open. Recent surveys and works on the Painlevé conjecture and on compactification of energy surfaces of n-body problems still cite the conjecture (nonwandering set nowhere dense in every energy level) as unresolved.

status_evidence.title: On Painlevé Conjecture (Xue)
status_evidence.snippet: For all energy E, the non-wandering set of the Hamiltonian flow on H^{-1}(E) is nowhere dense — attributed by Herman to Birkhoff and Kolmogorov, called the oldest problem in the Newtonian N-body problem.
status_evidence.claim: Conjecture is stated as a long-standing open problem in celestial mechanics.

status_evidence.title: Compactification of the Energy Surfaces for n Bodies
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on compactifying energy surfaces of the n-body problem motivated by the question of whether the nonwandering set is nowhere dense.
status_evidence.claim: The problem continues to motivate current research, indicating it is not solved.
